conventions.convention: Loops are smooth maps R/(2πZ) → g, where g is a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra. The symmetric invariant real bilinear form κ need not be nondegenerate, positive, simple or compact. The cocycle is ω(X,Y)=(2π)⁻¹∫κ(X,Y′)dθ, with differentiation on the second argument.

The extension bracket is [(X,a),(Y,b)]=([X,Y],ω(X,Y)); its central coordinates do not enter the right-hand side. A one-dimensional central extension does not require a nonzero cocycle or a nonsplit extension.

Species are finite-dimensional complex representations of the complexified real Lie algebra, all carrying a left-handed bookkeeping label. The label constructs no spinor field. The anticommutator is AB+BA without a factor 1/2; cubic and linear coefficients are separate representation traces.

The BRST obstruction statement is conditional on the supplier's specific Abelian jet complex, admissible counterterm subcomplex, nilpotent formal Ward operator and local breaking. It is not a construction for the general representation data and does not identify the trace coefficients with physical anomalies.
The opposite-charge example includes exactly two one-dimensional representations, with charges q and −q for any real q, each included once and both labelled left-handed.

load_bearing.statement: For a finite-dimensional real Lie algebra g and symmetric invariant real bilinear form κ, define smooth periodic loops with pointwise bracket, ω(X,Y)=(2π)⁻¹∫κ(X,Y′)dθ, and the candidate bracket [(X,a),(Y,b)]=([X,Y],ω(X,Y)).

For the data of def-qftx-loop-current-cocycle, ω is alternating and satisfies ω([X,Y],Z)+ω([Y,Z],X)+ω([Z,X],Y)=0. Consequently the candidate bracket is a Lie bracket and gives a one-dimensional central extension of the smooth loop algebra by R.

For the specified finite family of complex representations, define d^{abc}=Σᵢ tr(Tᵢᵃ{Tᵢᵇ,Tᵢᶜ}) and ℓᵃ=Σᵢ tr(Tᵢᵃ), with {A,B}=AB+BA. These are representation coefficients; the interface asserts no physical anomaly-cancellation criterion from d^{abc}.
